anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The engine allocates or leaks more RAM and swap than the host can safely provide, inflating buffer pools, plan caches, work areas, and background heaps until the operating system or the instance experiences memory pressure, paging, or OOM terminations.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on hot buffer-cache pages, latches, or I/O slots, producing excessive buffer-busy waits, CPU spin, and throughput stalls despite adequate raw CPU availability.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Persistent table or index pages become physically or logically corrupt—checksum failures, broken page links, or out-of-order keys—making on-disk structures unreliable and forcing retries, error handling, or full-scan fall-backs.

When all three anomalies surface together, the database alternates between memory exhaustion, low-level latch storms, and corruption-triggered retries. Symptoms include: 
• Rapid, uneven growth of the buffer cache and per-query work areas followed by OS paging or OOM kills.
• Spikes in buffer-busy/latch wait events as many sessions hammer a shrinking set of hot, repeatedly dirtied or corrupted pages that cannot be evicted promptly because memory is saturated and dirty-page flush queues are backlogged.
• Intermittent checksum or page-verification errors appearing alongside latch timeouts; queries that fall back from index access to full scans further inflate memory use and prolong latch holding times.
• Erratic performance: bursts of CPU spin mixed with periods of deep stalls while the engine retries failed I/Os, re-parses plans discarded under memory pressure, or restarts after crash recovery triggered by corruption or OOM.

Causal chain: Excessive memory allocation fills physical RAM, delaying or stalling background flushers. Dirty pages linger longer, increasing latch hold times and aggravating Buffer Cache and Latch Contention. Prolonged retention of dirty or repeatedly written pages raises the probability of torn writes during any forced restart or OOM kill, seeding Data Block and Index Integrity Anomalies. Conversely, encountering corrupted pages forces extra I/O retries, consistency checks, or full table scans, which allocate additional work memory and flood the buffer pool, amplifying memory pressure. The resulting feedback loop—memory overcommit → latch contention → corruption exposure → heavier memory and latch demand—degrades throughput, destabilizes the instance, and raises the risk of repeated crash-recovery cycles.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
